title: [P2] `scripts/model_sync.py --score` never returned a score when the model reasoned: deepseek-v4-flash spent the whole 4096-token budget on reasoning_content, content came back empty with finish_reason="length", and json.loads("") raised "Expecting value: line 1 column 1"
detail: Measured 2026-09-18 on the 12:00 local (17:00 UTC) scheduled run: step 3 of scripts/model_sync_cron.py ran `model_sync.py --diff --score` with a resolved DEEPSEEK_API_KEY and printed "❌ LLM scoring failed: Expecting value: line 1 column 1 (char 0)" — no reports/model_scores_*.yaml was written, so the day's candidate was never scored. Root cause isolated by direct probe against https://api.deepseek.com/v1/chat/completions with the script's own payload shape: model=deepseek-v4-flash, max_tokens=512, response_format=json_object returns http 200, finish_reason=length, content_len=0, reasoning_len=2432, completion_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens=512 — every token went to reasoning. The same probe against deepseek-v4-pro returned content_len=102 with 68 reasoning tokens, and deepseek-chat returned content_len=102 with 0 (both finish_reason=stop), i.e. the failure is the reasoning-budget shape on the flash model, not the prompt or the key. The old code had no retry, a fixed 4096-token budget, and json.loads(content) straight on the reply, so the condition was unrecoverable and un-diagnosable. FIX (7d7312c): _extract_json_object() parses fenced/prose-wrapped JSON and raises a ValueError that names empty-content vs no-JSON-object; _score_llm_reply() doubles the budget (8192 -> 16384 -> 32768) while finish_reason == "length" and hard-fails otherwise with model/finish_reason/budget in the message; request construction split into _score_request_body()/_post_score_request() so the ladder is testable through an injected poster. Live re-run of `model_sync.py --score` after the fix wrote reports/model_scores_20260918_1203.yaml (exit 0) with all 5 candidates scored.
reasoning: The auto-score path is the only producer of chimera.yaml-ready model entries for new candidates; it failed silently-to-the-catalog on a shape that recurs every time the scoring model reasons past its budget. Bane doctrine: auto-fix rather than let it sit broken. Fixed foreman-direct (no worker dispatch — the cron tick had the evidence and the blast radius was one function).

title: [P3] The first /v1/health after a server restart can still report timeout for a slow provider - the first litellm call of a fresh process costs ~10s of client/TLS warm-up, eating the whole health_timeout_s budget
detail: Measured 2026-09-18 tick 247 on a fresh server running e361802 (uvicorn + create_app factory, live chimera.yaml read-only, :8791). Hit 1 (cold process) took 10.01s wall and reported zai as {healthy: false, error: timeout: no response within 10.0s, error_class: timeout} with no model_tested - the same shape DF-CHIMERA-V2-16 fixed - while hits 2-5 (warm, ~8.3-9.0s wall) reported {error_class: quota, model_tested: z-ai/glm-5} with the provider's own 'Weekly/Monthly Limit Exhausted ... reset at 2026-09-20 04:07:32'. Same effect seen in the direct per-model measurement: the first probe of a fresh process cost 10.34s for one model, subsequent probes 2.75-3.19s. So the residual is client/TLS/provider-discovery warm-up inside litellm, not retry amplification (that half is fixed): one attempt can still exceed the shared 10.0s probe budget exactly once, at process start, and only for the provider that is currently failing. Impact: a monitoring check that fires immediately after a restart (or a deploy that restarts the service) reads a misleading timeout for one cycle; steady state is correct. FIX DIRECTION (pick one): warm the gateway once during startup before the server reports ready, or make the timeout branch distinguish 'task never produced a verdict' from 'provider answered late' (e.g. keep the partial verdict if the per-model attempt completed after the budget), or budget the probe per provider rather than one shared asyncio.wait window. PASS: on a freshly started server the FIRST /v1/health call reports the failing provider's real class (quota) rather than timeout, or the response explicitly marks the verdict as warm-up-uncertain.

detail: tests/test_release_workflow.py:1130 defines `requires_repo_venv = pytest.mark.skipif(not REPO_VENV_PYTHON.exists(), reason="the repo .venv (editable install) is required")` with REPO_VENV_PYTHON = REPO/'.venv'/'bin'/'python' (line 1128). The guard is evaluated at COLLECTION (module import), and pathlib exists() RAISES instead of returning False when a path component is not traversable, so a guard written to SKIP the module hard-aborts the whole session: "ERROR tests/test_release_workflow.py - PermissionError: [Errno 13] Permission denied: '/home/bunker-50887d8c/qa-chimera-v2/.venv/bin/python'" then "stopping after 1 failures" with ZERO tests executed from ANY module. Reproduced first-hand on the JIT agent: python3 -c 'from pathlib import Path; Path.home()/"qa-chimera-v2"/".venv"/"bin"/"python" .exists()' -> RAISED PermissionError [Errno 13]. Mechanism proven on the agent: the synced .venv/bin/python3.11 is an ABSOLUTE symlink to /home/kara/.local/share/uv/python/cpython-3.11-linux-x86_64-gnu/bin/python3.11 and /home/kara on the bunker host is mode 700 (drwx------), so stat() of the symlink chain returns EACCES. Reproduced locally in a self-contained non-root tree: .venv/bin chmod 000 -> exists() RAISED PermissionError, `python3 -m pytest -q` -> 'Interrupted: 1 error during collection', and a sibling module of trivially-passing tests never ran. Cells collapsed into this ONE cause: chaos-resource FAIL rc=1 in 3.58s (detail 'rc=1 under cap: ERROR tests/test_release_workflow.py - PermissionError'), the ci-pass native leg rc=1 in 5.17s (byte-identical log), and chaos-disconnect rc=1 in the same 1498-byte log whose OK verdict 'fails fast on disconnect' is a FALSE PASS - the rc came from the collection error before any disconnect handling was exercised. Fix shape: make the guard exception-safe (try/except OSError around .exists(), treating an unreadable path as absent) so a foreign or unreadable .venv skips that module instead of aborting the run.

title: [dogfood:P3] The /web/* chat path bypasses the response cache, the rate limiter and the queue backpressure that /v1/chat/completions enforces, so the same deliberation is billed twice over two surfaces with different protection
detail: Measured 2026-09-20 by reading both routers at live HEAD 4b89a9c. src/chimera/api/server.py calls _check_rate_limit(request, api_key) and await queue.acquire() in both /v1/deliberate (lines ~532/536) and /v1/chat/completions (~625/629); src/chimera/web/routes.py never calls either (grep -c for _check_rate_limit / queue.acquire / max_concurrent -> 0) even though session_chat() runs the same engine.deliberate() and bills the same providers. The asymmetry is invisible to a user because both surfaces return the same answer. FIX DIRECTION: route session_chat through the same RequestQueue and _check_rate_limit helper as the /v1 endpoints (the app state objects are already on request.app.state), keeping the SSE-side broadcast intact. title: [dogfood:P2] The board writer glues JSON rows when it appends to a file whose last line lacks a trailing newline: tasks.jsonl line 182 holds THREE tasks concatenated, so every line-wise reader (jq, the boardctl loader, the stand-in picker) sees one corrupt line and silently drops CH-GAP-055/056/057
detail: Found 2026-09-20 during a dogfood run while appending findings to the board. Evidence: .coding-hermes/board/tasks.jsonl line 182 is 8316 bytes and decodes as three objects back-to-back -- json.JSONDecoder().raw_decode at offset 0 yields CH-GAP-055 (0:2379), then CH-GAP-056 (2379:4657), then CH-GAP-057 (4657:8316) -- with no newline between them. 'json.loads' on that line fails with 'Extra data: line 1 column 2380'. The three rows are exactly the batch a board writer appended at 2026-09-20T08:35:00Z (the visible effects are in events.jsonl: id 1330 task_dispatched CH-GAP-056, id 1331 task_dispatched DEPS-004, same timestamp); the line BEFORE it ends without a trailing newline, which is the mechanism: 'f.write(json_line)' on a file whose last line is unterminated produces a glued line rather than two records, and a re-serialization of the untouched row then counts as a diff. HEAD (4b89a9c) parses clean -- 0 bad lines -- so this is a live writer defect, not committed damage: the corrupt line is uncommitted working-tree state. IMPACT: any line-wise consumer silently loses three tasks. Relevant to this project's own tooling -- the fleet board readers (boardctl, jq-based scans, the stand-in picker) all parse per line, so a glued line means rows exist in the file but not in any report, and the loss is invisible because the file looks fine to a human. PASS: appending to a board whose last line is unterminated yields zero 'Extra data' lines and a byte-identical prefix, with a regression test that starts from an unterminated file, appends, and asserts every line parses. NOTE for whoever repairs line 182: restore the three rows as three separate lines taken BYTE-EXACT from the current file (do not re-serialize -- a reserialization of the untouched rows pollutes the diff); this run deliberately did not rewrite them.
reasoning: Filed from a dogfood run, not as a code change: the dogfood lane must never edit the board beyond adding its own findings, so the glue was left in place with its byte offsets recorded. The defect class is general to the fleet (every JSONL board in the scheduler fleet has the same append-to-unterminated-file exposure).

Prime suspects to investigate (in order): (a) the stream for a session with recorded turns is intentionally REPLAYED-then-CLOSED (routes.py sse_stream, DF-CHIMERA-V2-19 policy) — if the SPA reconnects onto such a session or the send path does not re-establish a stream for the NEW turn, the connection is closing under it and EventSource re-dials forever; note sendMessage() sets deliberationComplete=false and clears retryTimer but never calls connectSSE(), so the stream live at send time is whatever was open BEFORE the turn existed; (b) a proxy/buffering layer between the browser and uvicorn (the fetch reader works, so plain HTTP streaming is fine — compare the two requests' headers/keep-alive handling); (c) `Connection: keep-alive` + `X-Accel-Buffering` semantics under the SPA's EventSource with HTTP/1.1 vs the fetch path.
